ambiguities.description: Optionality of Student enrollment: Is enrollment in an offering mandatory or optional for a student? The transcript states 'Students enroll in course offerings' but does not clarify whether every student must be enrolled in at least one offering, or whether a student can exist without any enrollments.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Optionality of grading: The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in', but does not clarify whether a grade is mandatory for all enrolled students or whether some students might be enrolled without receiving a grade (e.g., due to withdrawal or incomplete status).

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of course to course offering: The transcript confirms that one course can have multiple offerings, but does not clarify whether a single course must have at least one offering or whether a course can exist without any offerings.

source_references.excerpt: So the same course can have multiple offerings? Right. Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester. Intro to Databases might run in both Fall and Spring.

ambiguities.description: Optionality of instructor availability: The transcript states that 'Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor' and 'An instructor can teach several offerings', but does not clarify whether every instructor must teach at least one offering or whether an instructor record can exist without teaching any offerings.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor. An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Derivability of enrollment: It is unclear whether the enrollment relationship ('Student enrolls in Offering') should be objectified as its own entity type (e.g., 'Enrollment') with additional attributes like enrollment date or enrollment status, or whether it should remain a simple binary relationship. The transcript does not mention tracking enrollment-specific data such as enrollment date or enrollment status.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Constraint completeness on grading: The transcript confirms 'a student gets at most one grade per offering' but does not clarify whether a grade is mandatory (every enrolled student must receive a grade) or optional (some enrolled students might not receive grades due to withdrawal, incomplete, or audit status).
